unitTitle: Release Lifecycle and Patching: RU, RUR and Upgrades
title: Oracle Quiz

questions.question: In the Oracle Database patching lifecycle, what primary content distinguishes a Release Update Revision (RUR) from a standard Release Update (RU)?

answerOptions.text: RURs include new functional bug fixes from subsequent RUs, whereas RUs only contain security patches.
answerOptions.rationale: Release Updates (RUs) contain new functional bug fixes alongside security patches, whereas RURs exclude new functional bug fixes from subsequent RUs.

answerOptions.text: RURs deliver strictly critical security fixes and regression fixes for a specific RU without incorporating new functional bug fixes from subsequent RUs.
answerOptions.rationale: RURs are designed to extend an existing RU's lifespan by providing essential security and regression fixes while maintaining stability.

answerOptions.text: RURs modify major release numbers, while RUs only increment the database patch revision digit.
answerOptions.rationale: RUs increment the minor release version number, whereas RURs increment the patch revision digit.

answerOptions.text: RURs replace binary files in $ORACLE_HOME without requiring datapatch to update SQL dictionary metadata.
answerOptions.rationale: Both RUs and RURs require running datapatch to update data dictionary metadata after applying binary updates.

questions.hint: Think about which patch type is designed to extend an existing RU's lifespan with minimal functional change.

questions.question: How does applying a Release Update Revision (RUR) impact the Oracle Database version string compared to applying a Release Update (RU)?

answerOptions.text: Applying an RU increments the revision digit, while an RUR increments the minor version digit.
answerOptions.rationale: RUs increment the minor release version (such as 19.11 to 19.12), whereas RURs increment the revision digit.

answerOptions.text: Applying an RU increments the major release version, while an RUR increments the minor release version.
answerOptions.rationale: Major release version upgrades represent separate database releases rather than quarterly patch updates.

answerOptions.text: Applying an RU increments the minor version digit (e.g., 19.11 to 19.12), whereas an RUR increments the revision digit (e.g., 19.11.0 to 19.11.1).
answerOptions.rationale: RUs advance the database minor version, whereas RURs track maintenance iterations of a specific baseline RU.

answerOptions.text: Applying an RUR removes the version string completely from the dba_registry_sqlpatch view.
answerOptions.rationale: Database view dba_registry_sqlpatch records and displays detailed version and patch registry entries for both RUs and RURs.

questions.hint: Consider which digit changes when staying on a baseline RU while applying critical maintenance revisions.

questions.question: During the two-stage Oracle Database patching process, what is the primary role of the datapatch utility?

answerOptions.text: It replaces executable binaries, libraries, and header files inside $ORACLE_HOME while database services are stopped.
answerOptions.rationale: Binary replacement within the Oracle home is performed by opatch apply while database services are down.

answerOptions.text: It updates SQL metadata, data dictionary objects, and PL/SQL packages inside CDB$ROOT and all pluggable databases after reopening the database.
answerOptions.rationale: Datapatch automates post-patch SQL execution against data dictionary objects once the database is open.

answerOptions.text: It performs pre-patch conflict detection against active background processes while the database is mounted.
answerOptions.rationale: Conflict detection is an opatch pre-installation check performed prior to stopping services and applying binaries.

answerOptions.text: It automates the upgrade of the OPatch binary utility to its minimum required version.
answerOptions.rationale: DBAs must manually update OPatch to the minimum version specified in the patch Readme before running patch commands.

questions.hint: Recall which step occurs after binary patching has finished and database services are started.

questions.question: Which prerequisite action must a database administrator perform prior to executing binary patch installation using opatch apply?

answerOptions.text: Verify that OPatch meets the minimum required version in the Readme and perform conflict detection against $ORACLE_HOME.
answerOptions.rationale: Ensuring OPatch version compatibility and running conflict checks prevents partial patch applications and software issues.

answerOptions.text: Execute datapatch while the database is shut down to clear existing patch registry entries.
answerOptions.rationale: Datapatch requires the database to be open and cannot run while database services are down.

answerOptions.text: Convert the Oracle ASFU database license to an FU license to grant binary modification permissions.
answerOptions.rationale: Licensing models govern usage rights and third-party access, not binary patching mechanics.

answerOptions.text: Compile all PL/SQL packages across all pluggable databases using Oracle Data Pump.
answerOptions.rationale: Data Pump is used for data migration and export/import rather than pre-patch validation.

questions.hint: Consider what must be checked regarding the patching tool itself and existing software components before stopping services.

questions.question: Which database views allow a database administrator to inspect and confirm applied RU or RUR revision history in an Oracle Database environment?

answerOptions.text: v$instance and v$database
answerOptions.rationale: Views v$instance and v$database show general database instance status but do not track detailed SQL patch execution history.

answerOptions.text: registry$history and dba_registry_sqlpatch
answerOptions.rationale: These views maintain records of applied patch histories, SQL patch execution statuses, and database registry updates.

answerOptions.text: dba_tablespaces and dba_data_files
answerOptions.rationale: These catalog views store physical storage layout details rather than software patching registry information.

answerOptions.text: opatch_log_history and dba_patch_conflicts
answerOptions.rationale: These are not valid system views for inspecting applied database SQL patches.

questions.hint: Look for dictionary views specifically dedicated to registry history and SQL patch information.

questions.question: According to the patching lifecycle guidelines for IFS/Oracle environments, what is the primary recommendation for production systems with strict change-management policies?

answerOptions.text: Apply Release Updates (RUs) quarterly to introduce new functional enhancements immediately.
answerOptions.rationale: Broad functional changes in RUs increase execution plan variance, making them less ideal for locked production baselines.

answerOptions.text: Apply Release Update Revisions (RURs) to lock core execution behavior while maintaining security compliance between major upgrade windows.
answerOptions.rationale: RURs deliver critical security and regression fixes without altering broad application behavior or query execution plans.

answerOptions.text: Skip binary patching entirely and apply SQL updates only via datapatch.
answerOptions.rationale: Binary patching with opatch apply is required to update underlying executables before SQL scripts can be run.

answerOptions.text: Deploy RUs exclusively in production while applying RURs in non-production development environments.
answerOptions.rationale: RUs are recommended for non-production environments to test and validate functional updates before major upgrades.

questions.hint: Reflect on which strategy minimizes change scope and execution plan variance for mission-critical production systems.

questions.question: According to the table of contents of Oracle Database Database Upgrade Guide 19c, which tool is featured in Chapter 3 for database upgrades?

answerOptions.text: Database Upgrade Assistant (DBUA)
answerOptions.rationale: Upgrading with Database Upgrade Assistant (DBUA) is covered in Appendix C.

answerOptions.text: AutoUpgrade
answerOptions.rationale: Chapter 3 is dedicated to using AutoUpgrade for Oracle Database upgrades.

answerOptions.text: Parallel Upgrade Utility
answerOptions.rationale: Manual upgrades using Parallel Upgrade Utility are detailed in Chapter 4.

answerOptions.text: Oracle Data Pump
answerOptions.rationale: Data migration using Oracle Data Pump is covered in Chapter 9.

questions.hint: Appendix C covers DBUA and Chapter 4 covers the Parallel Upgrade Utility, so think about what Chapter 3 specifically focuses on.

questions.question: In Procedure 3 of cloud database migration for SAP on Oracle, which RMAN command creates an exact copy of the source database in the cloud without requiring a backup buffer?

answerOptions.text: opatch apply
answerOptions.rationale: The opatch apply command is used for applying software patches to an Oracle home, not database copying.

answerOptions.text: brbackup
answerOptions.rationale: The brbackup tool relies on backup files staged on file systems or cloud object storage.

answerOptions.text: duplicate database from active database
answerOptions.rationale: RMAN duplicate database from active database transfers data over the network directly from the active source to the target.

answerOptions.text: cross platform transportable tablespaces
answerOptions.rationale: Transportable tablespaces require staging backup files and metadata exports to a shared filesystem.

questions.hint: This procedure allows building an active copy directly over the network without stage-buffering export files or backups.

questions.question: Which procedure should be used when migrating an SAP Oracle database to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure across platforms with different endian types?

answerOptions.text: RMAN duplicate database from active database
answerOptions.rationale: Direct active database duplication requires compatible source and target platform endian formats.

answerOptions.text: RMAN cross platform transportable tablespaces command
answerOptions.rationale: Cross platform transportable tablespaces enable data movement between platforms with differing endianness.

answerOptions.text: BR*Tools brbackup with Object Storage
answerOptions.rationale: Standard BR*Tools backup and restore requires compatible operating system platform types.

answerOptions.text: OPatch binary staging procedure
answerOptions.rationale: OPatch updates executable software binaries in an Oracle home rather than migrating user database data across platforms.

questions.hint: Focus on the RMAN feature specifically designed to handle platform architecture differences like endianness.

questions.question: Which cloud database migration method for SAP on Oracle enables a transparent database upgrade as part of the data movement process?

answerOptions.text: RMAN duplicate database from active database
answerOptions.rationale: Database duplication creates an exact replica and does not support release upgrades during the duplication process.

answerOptions.text: Procedure 1 (RMAN via Object Storage)
answerOptions.rationale: Procedure 1 performs standard restore and recovery without executing transparent database version upgrades.

answerOptions.text: Oracle Lifecycle Migration Service (O2O / OOO)
answerOptions.rationale: O2O creates a new target database in the cloud, allowing transparent database upgrades during data transfer.

answerOptions.text: OPatch binary replacement method
answerOptions.rationale: OPatch applies interim patches and updates to an existing release rather than performing database release upgrades.

questions.hint: This service generates custom scripts to create a target database, allowing structural and feature adjustments during migration.

questions.question: What key functional difference distinguishes an Oracle Database with an Application Specific Full Use (ASFU) license from one with a Full Use (FU) license?

answerOptions.text: ASFU databases lack support for Oracle Advanced Security encryption features.
answerOptions.rationale: Oracle Advanced Security encryption is fully included in the SAP ASFU database license.

answerOptions.text: ASFU databases cannot be deployed on Oracle Exadata hardware.
answerOptions.rationale: ASFU databases are fully supported on Oracle Exadata systems and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.

answerOptions.text: ASFU databases may only be used by SAP ECC/NetWeaver applications, whereas FU databases allow access by non-SAP tools and third-party applications.
answerOptions.rationale: ASFU licensing restricts direct database access exclusively to the bundled SAP application suite.

answerOptions.text: ASFU license fees are calculated per processor core, whereas FU licenses are based on SAP contract percentages.
answerOptions.rationale: ASFU fees are calculated as a fixed percentage of the SAP contract, whereas FU licensing is based on processor cores.

questions.hint: Consider how license scope affects access to data from non-SAP software.

questions.question: What benefit is gained by incorporating Oracle GoldenGate into the Oracle Lifecycle Migration Service (changing O2O into the OOO procedure)?

answerOptions.text: It eliminates the requirement to execute post-patch SQL automation via datapatch.
answerOptions.rationale: Datapatch remains mandatory for updating dictionary metadata after binary patching regardless of data replication.

answerOptions.text: It captures changes made during data transfer, enabling online migration and reducing SAP downtime to a short switchover.
answerOptions.rationale: GoldenGate continuously replicates transactions so that the application remains online until the final switchover.

answerOptions.text: It automatically converts an ASFU database license into a public cloud FU subscription.
answerOptions.rationale: GoldenGate is a replication technology and does not alter database license classification rules.

answerOptions.text: It performs automatic cross-platform byte swapping without pausing database operations.
answerOptions.rationale: Byte swapping is handled by RMAN transportable tablespaces, not GoldenGate replication.

questions.hint: GoldenGate's real-time data replication allows application activity to continue while initial data movement is taking place.
